W2 (empirical), after E007.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete):
E001 9ep eager: 0.7430, 9.43s. E002 10ep eager: 0.7495, 10.55s. E004 compiled+fused SGD: 0.7486, 9.04s. E005 +Lookahead/EMA: 0.7583, 9.10s. E006 +Muon (bs2000): 0.7649, 9.45s. E007 +progressive res 24/28/32: 0.7590, 7.33s (best).

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: E001→E002 gives about +0.65 pp and +1.1 s per epoch (~12%). Almost all time scales with the work done, so fixed cost is small. One pair only, and probably concave.
2. Compile: E003's slowness was a recompile leak in timed code, and E004 fixed it (12.07→9.04 s). Warmup must match the training shapes and strides exactly. Progressive resizing worked without such a leak (E007 faster).
3. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s (E004→E005). It's the cheapest gain measured.
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s (E005→E006). Gain is real and costs about 4% time.
5. Progressive resizing: E006→E007 gives -2.12 s (-22%) for -0.59 pp. That is a very large time lever, and the accuracy cost is about one epoch's worth (~0.65 pp), so it is roughly a wash against the epoch dial per pp (1 epoch ≈ 1.1 s vs 2.1 s saved). Resizing wins on time per pp lost. Time scales with pixel count. Extrapolating, more aggressive shrinking should save further time, with accuracy falling faster below 24 px.
6. Margin: E007 is 0.60 pp above 0.753. Using 0.5-0.65 pp/epoch, about 0.5 epoch could be cut (~0.55 s at the current ~0.8 s/epoch).
7. Noise: accuracy 3-seed mean ±0.2 pp; time noise is unmeasured, probably 1-2%.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and resizing accuracy (I kept predicting refutes and they held). Lesson: ideas from the known speedrun literature transfer here better than my skepticism assumed.

Unsure: whether the EMA gain holds at fewer epochs; the 20 px floor; the Muon+EMA interaction with LR decay; and the real per-epoch time now (about 0.8 s).

forecasts.reason: Cutting 0.5 epoch costs about 0.3 pp and ~5% time; it likely stays above 0.753 but with a thin margin.
A lower final LR usually adds accuracy even with EMA, probably +0.3 pp; time is unchanged.
It saves about 1 s, but 20 px for 30% of steps costs accuracy, which lands near the bar.
Narrowing to 512 cuts last-group FLOPs by about 20%, so roughly 4% time, for a small accuracy loss.
A diagnostic with no recipe change; the seeds 3-12 mean is near the 0-2 mean, and the first epoch is probably slower than later ones.
Large batches mean little launch overhead; graphs help only the small-resolution steps, but risk breaking Muon's compiled update.
EMA'd BN stats are probably already close to right; the gain is likely under 0.3 pp, at a small time cost.

cruxes: What is the true per-epoch time and accuracy slope at E007 (about 0.8 s and 0.5 pp per epoch)? It sets how much margin can be cashed in.
Does accuracy collapse at 20 px (I011)? That decides whether resolution can keep cutting time.
What is the 40-seed accuracy versus the 3-seed mean (I013)? It decides how thin the margin may safely be.
